evidence: TaxRate.kind SIMPLE | GST; TaxSplitter hook in packages/accounting-engine computeDocument
TAX-001.notes: India GST is the first jurisdiction module. Other countries are not started.

TAX-005.notes: Registration (GSTIN format + check character), GST rates with categories (taxable, nil-rated, exempt, non-GST), place of supply on every GST document. GSTINs are not verified against the GST portal.

TAX-006.notes: Intra-state supplies: half the rate, rounded on its own, posted to Output/Input CGST.

TAX-007.notes: Intra-state supplies in states: posted to Output/Input SGST/UTGST.

TAX-008.notes: Inter-state supplies and exports (with payment of IGST): full rate to Output/Input IGST.

TAX-009.notes: Charged instead of SGST in union territories without a legislature (04, 26, 31, 35, 38, 97); shares the SGST/UTGST account.

TAX-010.notes: Invoices, credit notes, bills and vendor credits carry place of supply, supplier state, buyer/supplier GSTIN and tax by head; posted GST facts are immutable (DB trigger). Bills and vendor credits can be under reverse charge (the vendor is owed the amount without GST; the tax posts as output liability and input credit), including import of services from a vendor outside India (IGST). No PDF tax invoice layout or e-invoice IRN yet.

TAX-011.notes: 4, 6 or 8 digits, required on every GST line except non-GST. No HSN master or rate lookup; units of measure (UQC) are not tracked.

TAX-012.notes: ITC from bills less vendor credits, including reverse-charge tax and import of services (GSTR-3B 4(A)(2), 4(A)(3), 4(A)(5)), set off per CGST Act s.49/49A and rule 88A; reverse-charge tax is paid in cash (s.49(4)). Blocked credits (s.17(5)), reversals, ITC brought forward and GSTR-2B matching are not modelled.

evidence: apps/api/test/gst.e2e.test.ts › flags a manual journal on a GST account as a ledger difference
TAX-013.notes: GSTR-3B compares document totals with the movement on the six GST ledger accounts. Reconciliation with GSTR-2B is not built.

TAX-014.notes: GSTR-1 (B2B, B2CL, exports, B2CS, CDNR/CDNUR, nil/exempt, HSN B2B/B2C, documents issued) and GSTR-3B (3.1, 3.2, 4, 5, 6.1) working papers. Not the GSTN JSON format; nothing is filed.

TAX-053.notes: Decimal-only arithmetic; the web form runs the same engine as the API.

TAX-004.notes: India GST documents its rules, limitations, sources, tests and maintenance. No other country module exists yet.

TAX-017.notes: Income-tax Act 2025 s.393(1) templates (contractors, technical and professional fees, commission, rent, purchase of goods) or tenant-defined sections; single-document and aggregate thresholds per tax year or month, whole-amount catch-up or excess-only; PAN-based rates (individual/HUF, no-PAN). TDS on bills is worked out on the amount before GST, previewed in the form, posted to TDS payable and cuts what the vendor is owed. Register by quarter, challans (Dr TDS payable, Cr bank, optional interest) with void, and a ledger check. No lower-deduction certificates, no TDS on vendor credits or advances, no Form 26Q/140 file and nothing is filed.

TAX-018.notes: Tenant-defined TCS sections on invoices, worked out on the invoice value including GST and added to what the customer pays (TCS payable). Same register, challans and ledger check as TDS. No built-in TCS templates, no TCS on receipts, no Form 27EQ file.

TAX-022.notes: TDS and TCS challans are recorded with due dates (7th of the next month, 30 April for March) and overdue amounts. GST cash payments (PMT-06) and advance tax are not tracked yet. The compliance calendar shows each monthly TDS/TCS, PF, ESI and PT payment as done when its challan or payroll payment is recorded; advance tax and GST payments are marked paid/filed by hand.

TAX-037.notes: The engine supports one withholding (deduct or collect) per document with its own payable account; India TDS/TCS is the only jurisdiction configured.

PAY-001.notes: India payroll slice: employees, salary structures, monthly pay runs, payslips, ledger posting and statutory payments. Approvals, cost allocation, reporting and other countries are not built.

PAY-002.notes: Code, PAN (validated), UAN/ESI numbers, joining and leaving dates, work state, PT category, PF/EPS membership and previous-employer salary for the tax year. Identity fields freeze once a payslip is posted.

PAY-003.notes: Dated monthly structures (from the 1st of a month) with components marked as wages or excluded allowances under the Code on Social Security 2020; revisions are kept as history and a used structure cannot change.

PAY-005.notes: Components pro-rated by paid days; the 50% excluded-allowance add-back decides PF and ESI wages.

PAY-006.notes: Employee PF, ESI, Maharashtra professional tax and TDS on salary (new regime). No voluntary deductions, loans or advances.

PAY-007.notes: Bonuses can be added as one-off earnings on a payslip and are taxed in the month. No statutory bonus (Payment of Bonus Act) calculation.

PAY-011.notes: Loss-of-pay days (whole or half) per payslip, and pro-rating for joining or leaving mid-month. No leave balances or leave module.

PAY-016.notes: Posting a pay run journals gross salary and employer PF/ESI against net pay, PF, ESI, PT and TDS payables; voiding reverses it. Source PAYROLL.

PAY-017.notes: Records net-pay and statutory payments from a bank account with due dates (Dr liability, Cr bank). No bank transfer files, ECR or challan files.

PAY-018.notes: Printable payslip with earnings, deductions, employer contributions, income-tax working and year-to-date figures. No PDF or email delivery.

PAY-025.notes: PF/EPS/EDLI (with the Rs 25,000 ceiling from 17 Sep 2026), ESI, Maharashtra PT and new-regime TDS on salary. Not built: old regime, other states' PT, LWF, gratuity, perquisites. See docs/PAYROLL_INDIA.md.

PAY-026.notes: Every rate is cited to its source in the engine and on the settings page, but the rules have not been reviewed by a payroll professional; that review is required before real use.

TAX-023.notes: India compliance calendar: GST (monthly or QRMP, GSTR-9), TDS/TCS deposits and quarterly statements (Forms 138/140/143), PF, ESI, Maharashtra PT and advance tax, from the organisation set-up. Payments are settled by records in the books; returns are marked filed with the acknowledgement (void-only records). No holiday shifts or notified extensions; see docs/COMPLIANCE_CALENDAR_INDIA.md.

TAX-021.notes: Advance tax instalment dates (15/45/75/100%) are tracked and can be marked paid with the challan. The tax itself is not calculated.

PAY-004.notes: Payroll statutory due dates (PF, ESI, PT, TDS on salary, Form 138) are on the compliance calendar. No pay calendars or pay frequencies other than monthly.

TAX-015.notes: India e-invoicing for B2B invoices and credit notes: INV-01 (schema 1.1) JSON for the IRP, single and bulk; import of the IRP response checked against the document (IRN, seller, buyer, number, type, date, total) with optional RS256 signature check against a user-supplied IRP key; signed QR code drawn; 30-day reporting limit for AATO of Rs 10 crore and above; IRN cancellation recorded within 24 hours; a document with a live IRN cannot be voided (API and trigger). No direct IRP/GSP connection, exports, SEZ, debit notes, B2C QR or e-way bills; see docs/E_INVOICING_INDIA.md.

TAX-027.notes: Followed by design: Talk2Tax submits nothing to a government system. E-invoice JSON is uploaded by the user to the IRP and the IRP's response is imported; GST returns and TDS statements are marked filed by hand. An approved GSP/ASP integration is not built.
